name: Masters Tournament
description: Broadcast-quality Masters Tournament display with real ESPN player headshots, accurate Augusta National hole layouts, fun facts, past champions, live leaderboards, and pixel-perfect LED matrix rendering
author: ChuckBuilds

versions.notes: The 18 Augusta hole renderings are downscaled from roughly 4500x1800 to 768 pixels wide, which cuts the plugin's download from 207 MB to 5.8 MB and its hole images from 131 ms and 31 MB of RAM each to decode down to 5 ms and 1 MB. Nothing is drawn any smaller: a hole map is at most 248 pixels wide on the largest supported panel, so the old art was being thrown away at load. The cards are visually identical, under one part in 255 different on average. Also stops download_assets.py overwriting those renderings with the crude 200x150 schematics its fallback generator draws -- one run of that script used to replace the shipped artwork with no way back but a git checkout. It now fills in only the holes that are missing.

update_interval works below 30 seconds. The core scheduled update() at the manifest's 30 seconds and ignored a shorter configured interval; the plugin now returns the configured value from get_update_interval(). Requires LEDMatrix core 3.4.0, the first with the get_update_interval() hook; the store now refuses the install on older cores (on those the setting would stay ignored).

Mode registration changed: the core reads plugin.modes once, so a phase-built list never followed the calendar and a Pi started off-season never showed the leaderboard in Masters week. All fourteen modes are now registered, ordered from the phase lists (the off-season order first, so the off-season rotation is unchanged), and display() skips modes that are out of phase. Each skip makes the core log one INFO line ("display() returned False for mode ...") per rotation; that is expected. Repeated phase entries still weight an on-demand request; the core's normal rotation has always shown each mode once per cycle. The six display_modes.<mode>.duration settings now set that mode's time on screen, so with defaults the leaderboard shows for 25 s and featured holes for 15 s instead of display_duration (20 s). Stop presenting the mock leaderboard as real: it is used only with mock_data on, and when ESPN serves another event or a fetch fails with no good copy from the last day, the leaderboard modes skip. The fallback copy is stored without a ttl so it survives core 3.3.0's ttl-over-max_age rule. The countdown no longer fetches from display() and no longer shows NOW all off-season on stale meta. Headshots download in update(), not while drawing, after the schedule refresh; a failed download waits 10 minutes before retrying and ends that update's prefetch, so an unreachable image host costs one 5 s timeout per update instead of ten. VegasDisplayMode import guarded for cores before 3.1.0. Adds a manifest category.

Remove seventeen settings that nothing reads: the whole notifications and branding blocks, plus five leaves inside display_modes the generic mode handling never reaches -- player_cards.show_headshots and duration_per_player, course_tour.show_animations, duration_per_hole and featured_holes (#418). The README described Notifications and Branding as features; it no longer does. The masters_featured_holes display mode is unaffected -- it is a different thing from the course_tour.featured_holes config key.

versions.changelog: Render text 1-bit (no anti-aliasing) so glyphs stay crisp on the LED grid

versions.notes: Documentation. None of the 51 settings had a named key in the README; they were described in prose and JSON examples. All 51 are now documented at the paths the schema expects. Seventeen of them do nothing: the notifications block (8) and the branding block (4) are never read by the plugin or the core, and five leaves inside display_modes are read nowhere either, yet the README had sections presenting notifications and branding as features (#418). Adds real rendered screenshots of all fourteen display modes, produced with the plugin's own mock_data mode, split by tournament phase because eight render only during Masters week and six only outside it.

Make the player-card, hole, page and scroll-card sizing settings reachable in the web UI. The config form renders only the properties named in x-propertyOrder, so a setting the schema declares but that list omits was never drawn -- no field, no error, no hint it existed, and the only way to set it was to hand-edit config.json on the device. The values already validated on save and the plugin already read them; only the form was missing them.

Fix ESPN 403s. Around 2026-08-04 ESPN's site.api began rejecting both browser-style and bare custom User-Agent strings, which returned 403 Forbidden for every request this plugin made. Requests now send an identifying agent with the project URL, which ESPN accepts. No behaviour change beyond the header.

Config schema reorganized for a clearer setup experience: fine-tuning fields moved behind the web UI's collapsed Advanced Settings section (x-advanced). UX-only; no fields, defaults, or behavior changed.
